original_value: In this paper, we propose a novel blockchain‐based contractual routing (BCR) protocol for a network of untrusted IoT devices. In contrast to conventional secure routing protocols in which a central authority (CA) is required to facilitate the identification and authentication of each device, the BCR protocol operates in a distributed manner with no CA. The BCR protocol utilizes smart contracts to discover a route to a destination or data gateway within heterogeneous IoT networks. Any intermediary device can guarantee a route from a source IoT device to a destination device or gateway. We compare the performance of BCR with that of the Ad-hoc On‐Demand Distance Vector (AODV) routing protocol in a network of 14 devices. The results show that the routing overhead of the BCR protocol is 5 times lower compared to AODV at the cost of a slightly lower packet delivery ratio. BCR is fairly resistant to both Blackhole and Greyhole attacks. The results show that the BCR protocol enables distributed routing in heterogeneous IoT networks.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents a novel blockchain-based contractual routing (BCR) protocol for networks of untrusted IoT devices. Unlike conventional secure routing protocols that rely on a central authority (CA) to identify and authenticate each device, BCR works in a distributed way without a CA. It uses smart contracts to find routes to a destination or data gateway in heterogeneous IoT networks, and any intermediary device can ensure a path from a source IoT device to the destination device or gateway. We evaluate BCR against the Ad-hoc On-Demand Distance Vector (AODV) protocol in a 14-device network. The results indicate that BCR’s routing overhead is five times lower than AODV, though with a slightly reduced packet delivery ratio. BCR is also fairly resistant to Blackhole and Greyhole attacks, demonstrating distributed routing in heterogeneous IoT networks.
